sentences.arabic: الوطن العربي يمتد من الخليج للمحيط الأطلسي.
sentences.arabicTashkeel: الوَطَن العَرَبي يِمتَد مِن الخَليج للمُحيط الأطلَسي.
sentences.english: The Arab world stretches from the Gulf to the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.transliteration: il-watan il-3arabi yimtadd min il-khaleej lil-mu7eet il-atlasi.

sentences.english: We share the language, many traditions and the two Eids.

sentences.arabic: بس كل دولة إلها لهجتها، ومطبخها ولبسها التقليدي.
sentences.arabicTashkeel: بَس كُل دَولة إلها لَهجتها، ومَطبَخها ولِبِسها التَّقليدي.
sentences.english: But every country has its own dialect, cuisine and traditional dress.
sentences.transliteration: bas kull dawla ilha lahjat-ha, w-matbakhha w-libisha it-tagleedi.

sentences.arabic: الأكل العراقي يشبه أكل الشام، ولهجتنا قريبة من الخليج.
sentences.arabicTashkeel: الأكِل العِراقي يِشبَه أكِل الشّام، ولَهجتنا قْريبة مِن الخَليج.
sentences.english: Iraqi food resembles Levantine food, and our dialect is close to the Gulf.
sentences.transliteration: il-akil il-3iraaqi yishbah akil ish-shaam, w-lahjatna greeba min il-khaleej.

sentences.arabic: الدارجة المغربية مختلفة هواية، بس المصري مفهوم بكل مكان بفضل الأفلام.
sentences.arabicTashkeel: الدّارجة المَغرِبية مُختَلفة هْوايَة، بَس المَصري مَفهوم بكُل مَكان بفَضِل الأفلام.
sentences.english: Moroccan Darija is very different, but Egyptian is understood everywhere thanks to the films.
sentences.transliteration: id-daarja il-maghribiyya mukhtalfa hwaaya, bas il-masri mafhoom b-kull makaan b-fadhil il-aflaam.

sentences.english: This diversity is part of our identity.

sentences.arabic: بالبصرة، العادات تشبه الكويت؛ وبالموصل، تشبه سوريا.
sentences.arabicTashkeel: بالبَصرة، العادات تِشبَه الكُوَيت؛ وبالمَوصِل، تِشبَه سوريا.
sentences.english: In Basra, the customs resemble Kuwait; in Mosul, they resemble Syria.
sentences.transliteration: bil-basra, il-3aadaat tishbah il-kuwayt; w-bil-mawsil, tishbah soorya.

sentences.english: That's why Iraq is a meeting point of cultures.

scenario.situation: The student is at a dinner in Baghdad with an Iraqi, an Egyptian and a Lebanese colleague, and they start comparing their countries.
scenario.otherRole: An Iraqi colleague who loves comparing Arab cultures.
scenario.goalEnglish: Compare dialects, food, traditional dress and traditions across Arab countries, and talk about what is shared and what is different.
